html:
The Siege of Tobruk was a battle of the Second World War in 1941, when a garrison of mostly Australian troops held the Libyan port of Tobruk against German and Italian forces under Erwin Rommel for about eight months.

Tobruk's harbour was vital for supplies in the desert. The garrison held out behind minefields and was supplied by sea at night. It was relieved in late 1941. In June 1942 Rommel took the town in a day, a heavy blow to Britain, before his advance was stopped at the El Alamein in Egypt.

The desert war ruined Cyrenaica and left it full of mines. When it ended, Britain and France ran Libya until the UN made it independent under Idris.
